Scrolling Inside a Box

Tomato seedlings need steady warmth before they can be moved outdoors. A thin layer of compost keeps the soil moist through dry weeks.

A small telescope reveals the rings of Saturn as a delicate golden line. The Moon is slowly drifting away from the Earth by a few centimetres each year.

Maintenance crews inspect cables and bearings on a regular schedule. Wooden covered bridges were roofed to protect the timber from rain and snow.

After harvest, the ripe cherries are dried or washed to remove the fruit. Roasting changes the colour, aroma and flavour of the green beans.

Marigolds planted between the rows help to discourage some common pests. Rainwater collected in a barrel is gentler on young roots than tap water.

Dark skies far from cities make faint galaxies much easier to see. The planet Jupiter has more than seventy known moons.

Suspension bridges hang their decks from long cables anchored at both ends. Iron and later steel allowed builders to cross far wider rivers than before.

Freshly roasted beans are usually best within a few weeks. Many cafes now list the farm or cooperative that grew their beans.
